paragraphs: Hyatt Hotels Corporation is a global hospitality company with widely recognized, industry-leading brands and a tradition of innovation developed over our almost 70-year history.

Hyatt's portfolio of properties consists of full service hotels and resorts, select service hotels, all-inclusive resorts, and other properties, including timeshare, fractional, and other forms of residential and vacation units. We also offer distribution and destination management services through ALG Vacations and distribution services through Mr & Mrs Smith, a boutique and luxury global travel platform. On June 17, 2025, we completed the acquisition of Playa Hotels & Resorts N.V. ("Playa Hotels" or the "Playa Hotels Acquisition"), a leading owner, operator, and developer of all-inclusive resorts in Mexico, the Dominican Republic, and Jamaica. At December 31, 2025, our hotel portfolio consisted of 1,528 hotels and all-inclusive resorts (372,763 rooms). See Part II, Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Overview" for a breakdown of our portfolio. Our colleagues and hotel general managers are supported by our regional management teams, located in cities around the world, and our executive management team, headquartered in Chicago.

Our offering includes brands across five distinct portfolios. The Luxury Portfolio includes Park Hyatt, Alila, Miraval, Impression by Secrets, and The Unbound Collection by Hyatt; the Lifestyle Portfolio includes Andaz, Thompson Hotels, The Standard, Dream Hotels, The StandardX, Breathless Resorts & Spas, JdV by Hyatt, Bunkhouse Hotels, and Me and All Hotels; the Inclusive Collection includes Zoëtry Wellness & Spa Resorts, Hyatt Ziva, Hyatt Zilara, Secrets Resorts & Spas, Dreams Resorts & Spas, Hyatt Vivid Hotels & Resorts, Bahia Principe Hotels & Resorts, Alua Hotels & Resorts, and Sunscape Resorts & Spas; the Classics Portfolio includes Grand Hyatt, Hyatt Regency, Destination by Hyatt, Hyatt Centric, Hyatt Vacation Club, and Hyatt; and the Essentials Portfolio includes Caption by Hyatt, Unscripted by Hyatt, Hyatt Place, Hyatt House, Hyatt Studios, Hyatt Select, and UrCove. We also manage, provide services to, or license our trademarks with respect to residential units that are either for sale or owned by a third-party and participating in a voluntary rental management program, which are typically located within or adjacent to a Hyatt-branded full service hotel or in stand-alone developments. We consult with third parties on the design and development of such mixed-use projects. We license certain of our trademarks with respect to vacation units, which are part of Hyatt Vacation Club. We offer a short-term vacation rental platform, Homes & Hideaways by World of Hyatt, that features direct booking for short-term private home rentals in the United States ("U.S.").

We primarily derive our revenues from the provision of management, franchising, and hotel services, licensing of our portfolio of brands to franchisees and other hospitality-related businesses, including the Unlimited Vacation Club, operation of our owned and leased hotel portfolio, and provision of distribution and destination management services. For the year ended December 31, 2025, revenues totaled $7,101 million, net loss attributable to Hyatt Hotels Corporation totaled $52 million, and Adjusted EBITDA totaled $1,159 million. See Part II, Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Key Business Metrics Evaluated by Management—Adjusted Earnings Before Interest Expense, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization ("Adjusted EBITDA")" for our definition of Adjusted EBITDA, how we utilize it, why we present it, and material limitations on its usefulness, as well as a reconciliation of our net income (loss) attributable to Hyatt Hotels Corporation to Adjusted EBITDA for the periods presented.
We care for people so they can be their best. Our Vision
A world of understanding and care. Our Mission
We deliver distinctive experiences for our guests. Our Values
Empathy, experimentation, inclusion, integrity, respect, and wellbeing.

Our purpose, vision, mission, and values are brought to life by our colleagues, whom we refer to as the Hyatt family. We believe our colleagues around the world embody our purpose of caring for people so they can be their best. This includes caring for one another, our guests and customers, property owners, and the communities in which our properties operate. We are strongly committed to advancing care for all our stakeholders and creating personal connections to increase loyalty and drive results. High levels of guest satisfaction lead to increased guest preference for our brands, which we believe results in a strengthened revenue base over the long term. We also believe engaged colleagues will enhance the efficient operation of our properties, resulting in improved financial results. Sustained adherence to these principles is a basis for our brand reputation and strongly contributes to our growth as our diverse group of owners and developers choose to invest in our portfolio of properties around the world.

World of Care is our commitment to caring for people, the planet, and responsible business and a reflection of our purpose. Our World of Care pillars reflect our continuous engagement with colleagues, guests, customers, owners, investors, and communities to understand what is important to them. Through ongoing listening with these stakeholders and sharing information on our efforts, we strive to evolve our strategy and drive positive impact across communities.

•Caring for People: We care for the wellbeing of our colleagues, guests, customers, owners, and communities and are committed to advancing a culture of opportunity. Our efforts are focused on colleague development, wellbeing, human rights, inclusion, and community engagement and volunteerism.

•Caring for the Planet: As a global brand, we recognize that caring for the planet is integral to caring for people and we are committed to advancing environmental action. We seek to drive change in our communities with a focus on climate change and water conservation, waste and circularity, responsible sourcing, and thriving destinations.

•Caring for Responsible Business: Our commitment to caring for all our stakeholders drives what we do and how we work. It guides how we care for our people, communities, and planet, how we protect information and assets, how we demonstrate integrity in our business dealings, how we communicate honestly and transparently, and how we act as responsible professionals. Our Code of Business Conduct and Ethics reflects these commitments and provides a framework for making ethical business decisions.

We have significant competitive strengths that support our mission to deliver distinctive experiences for our guests and customers, drive growth, and create value for our colleagues, guests, customers, owners, and stockholders.

headings: Risks Related to the Hospitality Industry

Significant increases in the volume of sales made through third-party internet travel intermediaries could have an adverse impact on consumer loyalty to our brand and could negatively affect our revenues and profits.

If we are unable to establish and maintain key distribution arrangements for our properties or hospitality-related businesses, the demand for our rooms, hospitality-related services, and revenues could decrease.
We compete for guests, customers, management and hotel services agreements, franchise agreements, and residential and vacation units based on a variety of factors.
The risks of doing business internationally, or in a particular country or region, could lower our revenues, increase our costs, reduce our profits, or disrupt our business.
Labor shortages could restrict our ability to operate our properties or grow our business or result in increased labor costs that could reduce our profits.
Management and Hotel Services, Franchising, Ownership, Development, and Financing Risks
Contractual and other disagreements with third-party owners or franchisees could make us liable to them or result in litigation costs or other expenses, which could lower our profits.
Some of our existing development pipeline may not be developed into new hotels or may not open on the anticipated timeline, which could materially adversely affect our growth prospects.
Certain of our contractual arrangements with third-party owners require us to guarantee payments to the owners if specified levels of operating profit are not achieved by their hotels.
We plan to continue to sell selected properties; however, we may be unable to sell selected owned properties at acceptable terms and conditions, if at all.

paragraphs: In addition to the other information set forth in this annual report, you should consider carefully the risks and uncertainties described below, which could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.
The following is a summary of the principal risks and uncertainties described in more detail in this annual report:

•Global economic conditions and the cyclical nature of the hospitality industry could adversely affect demand for travel and lodging, and hospitality-related businesses, and, as a result, our revenues, profitability, and future growth.

•Risks relating to natural or man-made disasters, weather and climate-related events, contagious diseases, terrorist activity, and war could reduce the demand for lodging and hospitality-related businesses, which may adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
•We operate in a highly competitive industry, and our revenues, profits, or market share could be harmed if we are unable to compete effectively.

•New distribution channels, including potential AI platforms, alternatives to traditional hotels, significant increases in the volume of sales made through third-party internet travel intermediaries, and industry consolidation among our competitors could have an adverse impact on consumer loyalty to our brands and hospitality-related businesses and may negatively impact our business.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with Part IV, Item 15, "Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedule—Consolidated Financial Statements." For our discussion and analysis of our liquidity and capital resources for the year ended December 31, 2024, compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, see Part II, Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" of our 2024 Form 10-K. In addition to historical data, this discussion contains forward-looking statements about our business, operations, and financial performance based on current expectations that involve risks, uncertainties, and assumptions. Our actual results may differ materially from those discussed in the forward-looking statements as a result of various factors, including but not limited to those discussed in "Disclosure Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" and Part I, Item 1A, "Risk Factors" included elsewhere in this annual report.
At December 31, 2025, our hotel portfolio consisted of 1,528 properties (372,763 rooms), including:
•682 managed properties (204,841 rooms), including 127 all-inclusive resorts (45,385 rooms), all of which we operate under management and hotel services agreements with third-party owners;
•700 franchised properties (129,242 rooms);

•28 owned and leased properties (9,190 rooms), including 17 hotels (6,060 rooms), 6 operating leased all-inclusive resorts (1,262 rooms), 4 operating leased hotels (1,697 rooms), and 1 finance leased hotel (171 rooms), all of which we manage;
•21 managed properties and 2 franchised properties owned or leased by unconsolidated hospitality ventures (7,477 rooms);

•72 franchised properties (10,147 rooms) operated by an unconsolidated hospitality venture in connection with a master license agreement by Hyatt; including 6 properties (1,246 rooms) that are leased by the unconsolidated hospitality venture; and
•23 all-inclusive resorts (11,866 rooms) operated by a consolidated hospitality venture.
•22 vacation units (1,997 rooms) under the Hyatt Vacation Club brand and operated by third parties; and

•42 residential units (4,696 rooms), which consist of branded residences that are either for sale or owned by a third-party and participating in a voluntary rental management program and are typically located within or adjacent to a Hyatt-branded full service hotel or in stand-alone developments.

Additionally, we provide certain reservation and/or loyalty program services to hotels that are unaffiliated with our hotel portfolio and operate under other trade names or marks owned by such hotels or licensed by third parties. We also offer distribution and destination management services through ALG Vacations and distribution services through Mr & Mrs Smith, a boutique and luxury global travel platform.

We believe our business model allows us to pursue more diversified revenue and income streams balancing both the advantages and risks associated with these lines of business. Our expertise and experience in each of these areas give us the flexibility to evaluate growth opportunities across our lines of business. Growth in the number of management and hotel services agreements and franchise agreements and earnings therefrom typically results in higher overall returns on invested capital because the capital investment under a typical management and hotel services agreement or franchise agreement is not significant. The capital required to build and maintain hotels we manage, franchise, or provide services to for third-party owners and franchisees is typically provided by the owner of the respective property with minimal capital required by us as the manager or franchisor. In certain instances, Hyatt has provided funding to owners for the acquisition and development of hotels that Hyatt will manage, franchise, or provide services to in the form of cash, debt repayment or performance guarantees, preferred equity, or mezzanine debt. During periods of increasing demand, we do not share fully in the incremental profits of hotel operations for hotels we manage for third-party owners as our arrangements generally include a base fee that is, typically, a percentage of revenue from the subject hotel and an incentive fee that is, typically, a percentage of hotel profits (in certain circumstances, after satisfying certain financial return thresholds to be earned by the owner), depending on the structure and terms of the management and hotel services agreement. We do not share in the benefits of increases in profits from franchised properties because franchisees pay us an initial application fee and ongoing royalty fees that are calculated as a percentage of

gross room revenues, and also at times, as a percentage of food and beverage revenues, with no fees based on profits. Disputes or disruptions may arise with third-party owners and franchisees of hotels we manage, franchise, provide services to, or license to, and these disputes can result in the termination of the relevant agreement.

With respect to property ownership, we believe ownership of selected hotels in key markets enhances our ability to control our brand presence in these markets. Ownership of hotels allows us to capture the full benefit of increases in operating profits during periods of increasing demand and room rates. The cost structure of a typical hotel includes fixed costs, and therefore, as demand and room rates increase over time, the growth rate of operating profits typically is higher than the growth rate of revenues. The profits realized from our owned and leased hotels are generally more significantly affected by economic downturns and declines in revenues than the fee revenues earned from the properties we manage, franchise, or provide services to. This is because we absorb the full impact of declining profits for our owned and leased hotels, whereas our management and franchise fees do not have the same level of downside exposure to declining hotel profitability. Hotel ownership is more capital intensive than managing or franchising hotels for third-party owners and franchisees as we are responsible for the costs and capital expenditures for our owned and leased hotels. See also "—Principal Factors Affecting Our Results of Operations—Expenses" and Part I, Item 1A, "Risk Factors—Risks Related to Our Business—We are exposed to the risks resulting from investments in owned and leased real estate, which could increase our costs, reduce our profits, limit our ability to respond to market conditions, or restrict our growth strategy."

paragraphs: Hyatt Hotels Corporation 是一家全球性旅館業公司，擁有廣為認知、業界領先的品牌，並在近 70 年的歷史中累積了創新傳統。

Hyatt 的飯店組合包含全服務飯店與度假村、選擇性服務飯店、全包式度假村，以及其他類型的飯店，包括時尚分時度假、分額度假及其他形式的住宅與度假單位。我們也透過 ALG Vacations 提供旅遊行程的分銷與目的地管理服務，並透過 Mr & Mrs Smith 提供分銷服務，Mr & Mrs Smith 是一家精品與豪華全球旅遊平台。於 2025 年 6 月 17 日，我們完成了對 Playa Hotels & Resorts N.V.（"Playa Hotels" 或 "Playa Hotels Acquisition"）的收購，Playa Hotels 是墨西哥、多明尼加共和國與牙買加地區全包式度假村的主要所有者、營運者與開發商。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的飯店組合包含 1,528 家飯店與全包式度假村（共 372,763 房間）。請參閱 Part II, Item 7，"管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析—概覽" 以瞭解我們的組合細節。我們的同仁與飯店總經理由位於全球各城市的區域管理團隊與總部設於芝加哥的執行管理團隊提供支援。

我們的產品包含五大不同組合的品牌。奢華組合包含 Park Hyatt、Alila、Miraval、Impression by Secrets 與 The Unbound Collection by Hyatt；生活方式組合包含 Andaz、Thompson Hotels、The Standard、Dream Hotels、The StandardX、Breathless Resorts & Spas、JdV by Hyatt、Bunkhouse Hotels 與 Me and All Hotels；包容組合包含 Zoëtry Wellness & Spa Resorts、Hyatt Ziva、Hyatt Zilara、Secrets Resorts & Spas、Dreams Resorts & Spas、Hyatt Vivid Hotels & Resorts、Bahia Principe Hotels & Resorts、Alua Hotels & Resorts 與 Sunscape Resorts & Spas；經典組合包含 Grand Hyatt、Hyatt Regency、Destination by Hyatt、Hyatt Centric、Hyatt Vacation Club 與 Hyatt；基礎組合包含 Caption by Hyatt、Unscripted by Hyatt、Hyatt Place、Hyatt House、Hyatt Studios、Hyatt Select 與 UrCove。我們也管理、提供服務或授權我們的商標給參與自願租賃管理計畫的第三方所有或銷售的住宅單位，這些單位通常位於 Hyatt 品牌全服務飯店內或附近，或為獨立開發的項目。我們會與第三方合作，協助這些混合用途項目的設計與開發。我們也會授權部分商標給 Hyatt Vacation Club 的度假單位。我們提供一個短租度假平台，Homes & Hideaways by World of Hyatt，該平台提供美國（"U.S."）短租私人住宅的直接預訂服務。

本公司主要營業收入來自提供管理、特許經營及酒店服務，將我們的品牌組合授權予特許經營商及其他餐飲相關企業，包括無限假期俱樂部，經營我們自有及租賃的酒店組合，以及提供分銷及目的地管理服務。截至2025年12月31日財年，營業收入總計為7,101 百萬美元，歸屬於Hyatt Hotels Corporation的淨虧損為52 百萬美元，調整後的營業息稅折舊及 amortization（Adjusted EBITDA）為1,159 百萬美元。請參閱第二部分，第7項，"管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析—管理層評估的關鍵業務指標—調整後的營業息稅折舊及 amortization（Adjusted EBITDA）"，以瞭解我們對調整後的營業息稅折舊及 amortization（Adjusted EBITDA）的定義、我們如何運用此指標、為何我們會呈現此指標，以及此指標的使用限制，以及我們在所列期間內歸屬於Hyatt Hotels Corporation的淨收入（虧損）與調整後的營業息稅折舊及 amortization（Adjusted EBITDA）之間的調整關係。
我們關懷人們，讓他們成為最好的自己。我們的願景
一個充滿理解與關懷的世界。我們的使命
我們為旅客提供獨特的體驗。我們的價值觀
同理心、實驗精神、包容、誠信、尊重與身心健康。

本公司之目的、願景、使命與價值觀，透過我們的同仁實踐，我們稱這些同仁為希爾頓家族。我們相信全球的同仁體現了我們關懷人們使其成為最好的目的。這包括關懷彼此、客人與客戶、物業所有者以及我們物業運作的社區。我們致力於推動對所有利害關係人的關懷，並建立個人連結以提高忠誠度並推動成果。高程度的客人滿意度會導致客人對我們品牌的偏好增加，我們認為這會在長遠上強化營收基礎。我們也相信投入的同仁會提升物業運作的效率，進而改善財務表現。持續遵循這些原則是我們品牌聲譽的基礎，並強烈促進我們的成長，因為我們多樣化的所有者與開發者選擇投資我們在全球的物業組合。
World of Care 是我們對關懷人們、地球與負責任企業的承諾，並反映我們的宗旨。我們的 World of Care 柱石反映我們持續與同仁、客人、客戶、所有者、投資者與社區互動，瞭解對他們而言什麼是重要的。透過持續與這些利害關係人溝通並分享我們努力的資訊，我們致力於進化我們的策略，並在社區中推動正面影響。
•關懷人們：我們關懷同仁、客人、客戶、所有者與社區的福祉，並致力於推動機會文化的發展。我們的行動聚焦於同仁發展、福祉、人權、包容性與社區參與及志工服務。
•關懷地球：作為一個全球品牌，我們認知到關懷地球是關懷人們的關鍵，我們致力於推動環境行動。我們希望在社區中推動改變，重點在氣候變遷與水資源保存、廢棄物與循環經濟、負責任的採購以及繁榮的旅遊目的地。
•關懷負責任企業：我們對所有利害關係人的關懷承諾，驅動我們的行動與工作方式。這指導我們如何關懷同仁、社區與地球，如何保護資訊與資產，如何在商業往來中展現誠信，如何誠實透明地溝通，以及如何作為負責任的專業人士。我們的商業行為準則與倫理規範反映這些承諾，並提供一個做出倫理商業決策的框架。
我們擁有重要的競爭優勢，支持我們實現為客人與客戶提供獨特體驗、推動成長，並為同仁、客人、客戶、所有者與股東創造價值的使命。

paragraphs: 下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，應與第四部第十五項「附屬文件及財務明細表—合併財務報表」一併閱讀。有關我們於2024年12月31日財年與2023年12月31日財年比較之流動性及資本資源之討論與分析，請參閱第二部第七項「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」於我們2024年Form 10-K中。除歷史資料外，本討論包含有關我們業務、營運及財務表現之展望性陳述，基於目前預期，涉及風險、不確定性及假設。我們實際結果可能與展望性陳述中所述有重大差異，原因包括但不限於「關於展望性陳述之揭露」及第一部第一A項「風險因素」中所討論之因素。
於2025年12月31日，我們之飯店投資組合包含1,528個飯店（372,763間客房），包括：
•682個由我們管理之飯店（204,841間客房），包括127個全包式度假村（45,385間客房），所有這些均由我們與第三方所有者簽訂之管理及飯店服務協議下運作；
•700個特許經營之飯店（129,242間客房）；
•28個自有及租賃之飯店（9,190間客房），包括17間飯店（6,060間客房）、6間運作租賃之全包式度假村（1,262間客房）、4間運作租賃之飯店（1,697間客房），以及1間財務租賃之飯店（171間客房），所有這些均由我們管理；
•21個由未合併之飯店合作企業擁有或租賃之管理飯店及2個特許經營之飯店（7,477間客房）；
•72個由未合併之飯店合作企業根據Hyatt之總特許經營協議運作之特許經營飯店（10,147間客房）；包括6個由未合併之飯店合作企業租賃之飯店（1,246間客房）；以及
•23個全包式度假村（11,866間客房）由合併之飯店合作企業運作。
•22 假日俱樂部單位 (1,997 房間) 係屬 Hyatt Vacation Club 品牌，並由第三方經營；以及
•42 套住宅單位 (4,696 房間)，其為品牌住宅，這些住宅或是待售，或是由第三方所有並參與自願租賃管理計畫，通常位於 Hyatt 品牌全服務酒店內或附近，或為獨立開發項目。
此外，我們亦為與我們酒店組合無關聯的酒店提供部分預訂及/或忠誠度計畫服務，這些酒店使用其他品牌或標誌，或是由這些酒店所有或由第三方授權。我們亦透過 ALG Vacations 提供分銷及目的地管理服務，並透過 Mr & Mrs Smith 提供分銷服務，Mr & Mrs Smith 是一家精品與豪華全球旅遊平台。

我們相信我們的商業模式使我們能追求更多元化的收入與獲利來源，平衡這些業務線的優點與風險。我們在這些領域的專業知識與經驗，使我們能靈活評估各業務線的成長機會。管理與酒店服務協議及特許經營協議數量的增加與相關獲利，通常會導致整體投資資本的回報率提高，因為典型的管理與酒店服務協議或特許經營協議所需的資本投資並不大。我們管理、特許經營或為第三方所有者與特許經營者提供服務的酒店所需建設與維護的資本，通常由該酒店的擁有者提供，我們作為管理公司或特許經營商所需的資本則極為有限。在某些情況下，Hyatt 會為擁有者提供資金，用以取得或開發 Hyatt 將管理、特許經營或提供服務的酒店，資金形式包括現金、債務償還或績效保證、優先股或中期債務。在需求增加的時期，我們通常不會完全分享由第三方擁有者管理的酒店營運利潤的增量，因為我們的協議通常包含一筆基本費用，通常是該酒店營收的百分比，以及一筆激勵費用，通常是酒店利潤的百分比（在某些情況下，需先滿足擁有者應達成的財務回報門檻），視管理與酒店服務協議的結構與條款而定。我們不會分享特許經營物業利潤增加的效益，因為特許經營商會支付我們一筆初始申請費用及持續的 royalty 費用，這些費用計算為客房營收的百分比，有時也會計算為餐飲營收的百分比，而沒有基於利潤的費用。
與第三方擁有者及特許經營商就我們管理、特許經營、提供服務或授權的酒店可能產生爭議或中斷，這些爭議可能會導致相關協議終止。

關於物業所有權，我們認為在關鍵市場擁有部分酒店有助於我們控制這些市場的品牌存在。擁有酒店使我們能完全享有在需求增加及房價上漲期間營運利潤的增長。典型酒店的成本結構包含固定成本，因此，隨著需求及房價隨時間增加，營運利潤的增長率通常高於營收的增長率。我們所擁有及租賃的酒店所產生的利潤，通常比我們管理、特許經營或提供服務的物業所產生的費用收入更受經濟衰退及營收下降的影響。這是因為我們會完全吸收我們所擁有及租賃酒店營運利潤下降的影響，而我們的管理及特許經營費用則不會有相同程度的下行風險。擁有酒店比為第三方擁有者及特許經營者管理或特許經營酒店更具資本密集性，因為我們需承擔我們所擁有及租賃酒店的成本與資本支出。請參閱 "—主要影響我們營運結果的因素—費用" 以及第一部分，項目 1A，"風險因素—與我們業務相關的風險—我們面臨因投資於自有及租賃實體資產而產生的風險，這可能會增加我們的成本、減少我們的利潤、限制我們對市場條件的反應能力，或限制我們的成長策略。"

headings: 與本公司業務相關的風險
若透過第三方網路旅遊中介平台的銷售量大幅增加，可能會對消費者對本公司品牌的忠誠度產生負面影響，並可能對本公司營業收入與利潤造成不利影響。
若本公司無法建立並維持關鍵的銷售管道安排，用以銷售本公司旗下的飯店與餐飲相關業務，則對本公司客房、餐飲相關服務及營收的需求可能會減少。
本公司與其他競爭對手爭取旅客、客戶、管理服務契約、特許經營契約以及住宅與休閒單位，係基於多種因素進行競爭。
國際業務或特定國家或地區的營運風險，可能降低我們的營業收入，增加我們的成本，減少我們的利潤，或幹擾我們的業務。
人力短缺可能限制我們運營物業或擴張業務的能力，或導致勞動成本增加，進而減少我們的利潤。
管理與酒店服務、特許經營、所有權、開發及融資風險
與第三方所有者或特許經營商的契約及其他爭議，可能使我們對他們負有責任，或導致訴訟成本或其他費用，進而降低我們的利潤。
我們現有的開發項目中，部分可能無法開發成新酒店，或無法按預期時間表開幕，這可能會對我們的成長前景造成重大不利影響。
我們與第三方所有者之間的某些契約安排要求，若其酒店未達成指定的營運利潤水平，我們需保證支付給所有者。
我們計畫繼續出售部分物業；然而，我們可能無法以可接受的條件和方式出售部分自有物業，甚至可能無法出售。
經濟及其他條件可能對我們造成不利影響
paragraphs: 除本年度報告中所載之其他資訊外，您應謹慎考慮下列所描述之風險與不確定性，這些因素可能會重大且不利地影響本公司之業務、財務狀況、營運成果及現金流。
下列為本年度報告中更詳細說明之主要風險與不確定性摘要：
•全球經濟情勢及旅館業之週期性特質，可能會不利地影響旅遊與住宿需求，以及與旅館相關之業務，進而影響本公司之營業收入、獲利能力及未來成長。
•與自然或人為災難、天氣與氣候相關事件、傳染病、恐怖攻擊及戰爭相關之風險，可能會降低住宿與相關旅館業務之需求，進而對本公司之財務狀況與營運成果造成不利影響。
•本公司所處之產業為高度競爭，若本公司無法有效競爭，可能會對本公司之營業收入、利潤或市佔率造成損害。
•新興之分銷渠道，包括潛在之AI平台、傳統旅館之替代方案、透過第三方網路旅遊中介所進行之銷售交易量大幅增加，以及競爭對手之間之產業併購，可能會對本公司品牌與相關旅館業務之消費者忠誠度造成不利影響，並可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
